proposer_change.change: In QUALITY, add 'Write each 300-word section as two paragraphs of nine to ten concise sentences (14 to 17 words each, at least 285 words per section).' while keeping VOCABULARY and every other line of round-002.md identical.
proposer_change.why: Round 2 champion train unique_sentences averaged 48.833 against the 146.7 real reference, and Round 5 showed that concise sentences raised train unique_sentences to 65.833 while only increasing commercial_per_k to 4.782 when sections were split into four or five paragraphs.

writer_notes: Round 14 passed all hard qualification and retrieval gates on both train and holdout (zero violations) with four fresh writer subagents running from scratch.
Train unique_sentences improved from 48.833 to 62.667 (+13.8 sentences per file, with 104 and 87 unique sentences on DOCX and 89 and 73 on PDF).

However, two effects worsened commercial_per_k (3.482 vs 2.257) and top_opener_share (0.166 vs 0.130): first, under round-002.md VOCABULARY (name each commercial measure at most once in a paragraph), writers named both gross profit and gross margin in both paragraphs of each PDF section (14 matches per PDF file vs 7 in Round 2); second, writing PPTX slide sections as two paragraphs instead of three caused the PPTX slide renderer (which takes the first sentence of each paragraph as a bullet) to extract only two bullets per slide, reducing PPTX total sentences from 16 to 10 so five slide date footers (# April #) accounted for 50% of PPTX sentences.
Therefore policies/writer/round-002.md remains the promoted champion policy.
